routing_warnings.description: The request for a Danish interactive-field label concerns field-label wording rather than the template language configuration.
The specified Danish date placeholder is field-specific placeholder content.
The clarification supplies separate Danish placeholder text for the date and subject fields.
The rejected Master-template feedback concerns malfunctioning elements and is subsequently clarified as a table-component problem rather than a failure of the shared master-template architecture.
The reported nonfunctioning tables concern Master-template table components rather than whether derived templates use a shared master foundation.
The request to reduce spacing so the document fits on one page changes spacing behavior rather than legacy copy-paste stability.
The request to omit the first-page footer number and begin numbering on page two belongs to the page-numbering Requirement.
The question concerns the font size and emphasis of Title and Heading 1 rather than style-system completeness.
The implementation activity concerns spacing configured for individual styles.
The reported break after three bullets concerns list behavior rather than whether the style catalog is consistently present.
The missing theme-colors clause independently supports the controlled theme-color Requirement.
The missing image/table label typography clause independently supports the typography Requirement.
The missing green level-four bullet clause independently supports the bullet-formatting Requirement.
Using the New Styles document as the master template concerns the shared master-template foundation.
Using the new master template as the basis for other documents concerns the shared master-template foundation.
The acceptance also resolves the immediately preceding proposal that the document be configured with English as its default language, which affects the separate language-configuration Requirement.
The first sentence reports numbered-list alignment breaking at 10 and belongs to the numbered-list alignment Requirement.
The observed break after three bullets concerns list continuation behavior rather than style typography.
The missing green level-four bullet is evidence for bullet visual formatting.
The missing theme colors are evidence for the controlled theme color palette.
The report that bullet sizes look wrong concerns bullet visual formatting rather than general style typography.
The list breaking after three bullets is associated with Tab and style-ribbon use in the adjacent context, rather than with bullet appearance.
The freelancer attributes the bullet behavior to use of Tab instead of the style ribbon, which concerns list-level transitions rather than the approved visual bullet design.
The separate clause requiring Overskrift 3 to become bold concerns template typography, not numbered-list alignment.
The list breaking after three bullets is linked by nearby messages to using Tab and the style ribbon, making hierarchy behavior a better target.
The client explicitly reports using only the Tab key, which concerns Tab-driven list hierarchy rather than multi-digit numbering alignment.
This message identifies which template style users should select for numbering but does not establish that numbered-list alignment was implemented or verified.
This message identifies the green numbering style but does not report an alignment change, fix, or runtime result.
The inability to use Enter in a right-side text area concerns ordinary multiline text entry, not creation of a new list item.
The reported Enter result concerns multiline entry across text fields and includes a remaining field-specific failure.
The claim that Enter now works everywhere addresses multiline text entry rather than automatic list continuation.
The headline Enter failure concerns multiline headline entry, not creation of a bullet or numbered item.
The client accepts adding Enter support to the headline field, which is a multiline text-entry change.
The requested table design concerns inclusion of the template's visual style system rather than operation of reusable table components.
The request for a walkthrough explaining how Master-template tables function is a usage-guidance deliverable.
The statement about manually resizing a content checkbox concerns checklist-control behavior rather than whether Master-template tables function without breaking or duplicating content.
The implementation claim that top and bottom spacing was configured for three designs concerns spacing rather than Master-template table-component operation.
The reported inability to use Enter concerns whether multiline input is accepted, not the spacing produced by an accepted hard return.

The concrete result that Enter works except in one field concerns multiline-entry support; the separate spacing question does not identify continuous-text hard-return spacing clearly enough for this target.

The claim that Enter now works everywhere directly concerns multiline-entry support; its broad top-and-bottom spacing claim does not specifically entail corrected hard-return spacing in continuous text.
The statement that Enter works everywhere except the last field concerns multiline text entry; only the separate spacing clause applies to fixed layout margins.
This message concerns retention of the specialized Bestyrelsesmode dropdown rather than ordinary text placeholders.
This message concerns retention of the specialized Indstilling checklist rather than ordinary text placeholders.
The message reports that a field placeholder does not clear when clicked, which concerns activation behavior rather than help labels.
The message reports formatting loss in the Title field rather than a help-label issue.
The requested automatic removal of field text on activation belongs to the independently tracked clear-on-activation behavior.
The request concerns automatic placeholder removal when a field is clicked or activated.
The message explains a field activation and typing path rather than changing or verifying help-label behavior.
The message explains that existing text must be deleted on one activation path, which concerns placeholder clearing.
The clear-on-click feedback clauses concern placeholder activation behavior; the remaining clauses in the message belong to other independent Requirements.
The message reports that a placeholder does not clear when clicked, which concerns activation behavior rather than visual identification.
The message reports formatting loss in a title field rather than a failure of visible input cues.
The placeholder-field observation reports failure to clear text on activation, not failure to visually identify fillable areas.
This message reports that clicking most fields clears their placeholder text; it does not address preservation of field formatting.
This message concerns inconsistent field activation and typing behavior rather than typography or formatting preservation.
The Danish date prompt changes the date field's help or placeholder label rather than its calendar-selection behavior.
This message distinguishes date and subject placeholder wording and is better routed to the interactive field help-label Requirement.
This message clarifies the Board Meeting field-alignment defect rather than the row-insertion workflow.
This message defines the row-insertion and field-copying workflow itself, but does not explicitly require that workflow to be included in the guidance artifact.
The claim that 0.06 spacing was applied to every row and column concerns structured spacing rather than verification that overflowing text wraps or columns remain within the page.
The Board Meeting misalignment observation concerns alignment among named fields rather than table-paste or overflow stability.
The report that Master Template tables are not functioning and may duplicate text concerns reusable master-table components rather than column geometry during content growth.
The applied row-and-column spacing addresses structured content spacing rather than containment of an overflowing column.
The Board Meeting alignment observation concerns alignment among named fields rather than column overflow containment.
The client clarifies the Board Meeting field-alignment defect, which belongs to the dedicated alignment Requirement.
The request to reduce spacing specifically so the copied content fits on one page is better routed to the independently defined page-fit spacing Requirement.
The report that bullet sizes and spacing look wrong concerns bullet visual formatting rather than general structured-content spacing.
The excessive hard-return spacing for continuous text belongs to the independently defined continuous-text line-spacing Requirement.
The clause reporting that Enter works everywhere except the last field concerns multiline text-entry behavior; only the separate spacing clause applies to the target Requirement.
The claim that Enter now works everywhere concerns multiline text-entry behavior.
The claim that margins will no longer collapse concerns fixed layout margins.
The manual-line-break issue in this message is specifically tied to pasted legacy content and is better routed to the post-paste line-break Requirement.
The reported excessive spacing from hard returns concerns continuous-text spacing rather than the ability to insert a line break after legacy content is pasted.
The inability to use Enter inside the right-side text area concerns general multiline field entry, with no stated legacy-paste context.
This reports that Enter fails in one field and belongs to the general multiline-entry Requirement.
The claim that Enter now works everywhere addresses general multiline entry rather than post-paste line-break behavior.
The headline-specific Enter failure concerns general multiline field entry and does not mention pasted content.
The client confirms that an Enter option is required for the headline, which modifies the scope of general multiline entry.
